content.text: Both preferred elements are met, with no competing forum or arbitration provision anywhere in the document.

input.quote: 28.2 The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 makes New York law the governing law (with CISG expressly excluded), and Section 28.2 gives the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction with irrevocable submission and a venue/forum-non-conveniens waiver. This sits at our preferred position, not merely the fallback. The carve-out permitting temporary injunctive relief in another court is customary and does not defeat the exclusive merits forum, and the pre-filing executive escalation in 28.3 expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-preserving filings. No arbitration clause (foreign-seated or otherwise) or competing forum appears anywhere in the document. No redline needed.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
mappings.quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.

mappings.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
